title: AFSI / AFT / Carl Zeiss Meditec / Afya / AGCO / Arctic Glacier / AUTO1 / Algoma Steel — Business vs Security, Short Timing and Entry Price V9

notes: Raw Short -> actual Long corrections: AFT-U 2004 and AG1 2021.
AFT-U 2004 and AG-U 2009 are Canadian income-trust units rather than ordinary corporate common shares.
No source-DB horizon performance rows were available for these ten ideas; outcomes rely on primary operating data, takeover consideration, insolvency distributions and historical price cross-checks.
AFSI 2013 accounting concerns were partly validated by 2017 restatements, but the stock nearly doubled against the short before the catalyst and was ultimately taken private at $14.75.
Advanced Fiber Technologies was acquired by Aikawa in 2006 for C$3.00/unit versus the VIC entry around C$5.50; distributions reduce but do not eliminate the loss.
Carl Zeiss Meditec maintained important product franchises but failed the original earnings and valuation path; FY2024/25 EPS was €1.61 and 2025/26 profitability weakened further.
Afya delivered strong revenue, EBITDA and free-cash-flow growth but did not achieve the original public-market rerating; the 2026 share price remains around the 2022 entry level.
AGCO 2003 offered a medium-term favorable short move by 2005, but the business expanded rapidly and the stock later surged. AGCO 2005 was a clear short failure during the ag upcycle.
Arctic Glacier entered CCAA in 2012. Later mixed-currency distributions were far below the C$1.72 entry and are not simplistically summed without FX dates.
AUTO1 2021 and 2022 demonstrate entry-price dependence: the same business execution produced a loss from ~€31.6 but a large gain from ~€10-11.
Algoma Steel was acquired by Essar in 2007 for C$56 cash/share versus the 2003 VIC entry at C$3.30, about 17x.

batch_lessons: Fundamental accounting concerns can be correct while a short still fails because catalyst latency and adverse excursion dominate security-level returns.
An M&A catalyst is only valuable at the actual takeout price; strategic interest is not a valuation floor.
A strong medical-device moat does not prevent large losses when earnings duration and starting multiples are overestimated.
Operating growth can compound for years without equity rerating when country and regulatory risk premiums persist.
Cyclical shorts require a cycle-inflection thesis in addition to leverage analysis.
Stable operating cash flow is not sufficient protection for equity when refinancing fails before liabilities mature.
The same company can be a bad investment at one price and a good investment at another; AUTO1 2021 vs 2022 is a clean example.
Future terminal targets should be tracked provisionally until their stated horizon has arrived.
Post-reorganization equities can produce extreme convexity when fixed claims are reset but operating leverage remains.
Corporate takeout consideration, insolvency distributions and actual capital structure take precedence over narrative valuation.
